reasoning_traces.think:
The playerElo framework addresses a fundamental limitation in traditional sabermetrics—namely, that metrics like wOBA, wRC+, and xwOBA do not adequately control for strength of schedule. This oversight leads to misleading comparisons between players who perform under vastly different levels of competition. By integrating run-value expectations into an Elo-based system, playerElo dynamically adjusts player ratings based on the quality of competition encountered. Each at-bat contributes to a player’s evolving rating through a differential update rule: if a batter performs better than expected against a high-quality pitcher, their Elo increases more than if they performed similarly against a weak one. Similarly, pitchers are credited or penalized depending on how well they perform relative to expectations. The model computes expected run values from base-out states and compares them to actual outcomes, adjusting ratings accordingly. This process inherently factors in situational context, such as park effects and home-field advantages, making it robust to environmental variability. In GSI, this translates to Bayesian inference over player skill, where prior beliefs about performance are updated with empirical data. In GSE, it enables simulation of strategic decisions under varying competitive pressures. The method avoids conflating team strength with individual ability, offering a clearer lens for evaluating talent in free agency or trade scenarios.
